title: Set 02 — Healthy Habits, Markets and Solar Energy
p1: Sadia gets up early and drinks a glass of water before breakfast. She walks to school with her cousin because the road is safe and the distance is short. At school she plays games during the break. Her mother packs fruit and homemade bread for lunch. In the afternoon, Sadia finishes her homework and spends some time outdoors. She knows that healthy food, physical activity and enough sleep help children stay active and cheerful.

p2: Our weekly village market opens on Friday morning. Farmers arrive with fresh vegetables, eggs and rice. Buyers compare prices before choosing what they need. Amina carries a reusable bag to reduce waste. She speaks politely with sellers and checks that the food is clean. By midday the market becomes quieter, and many farmers return home. The market helps families buy fresh food and supports local workers.
unseen: A school in a small town installed solar panels on its roof in June. The panels make electricity from sunlight. On sunny days, the school uses this electricity to run lights and fans in four classrooms. Science teacher Mr Hasan showed students how the system works. They measured the energy produced over five days and made a wall chart. The project encourages students to use energy carefully.

summary: A small-town school placed solar panels on its roof in June. These panels turn sunlight into electricity for lights and fans in four classrooms. Mr Hasan explained the system. Students observed the energy produced for five days and created a chart. The project teaches responsible energy use.
